title: LTS channel interop scenarios and upgrade safety checklist
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: Define a concrete interop matrix and a reusable safety checklist for rolling LTS channel upgrades across the runtime, public API, client SDKs, and Console. This ticket captures the scenarios we must support, the gating criteria for staged rollouts, and the automated/tooling requirements for safe upgrades and quick rollback.

Scope: runtime (inference engine + kernel selection), Redwood API (REST/streaming), SDKs (Python/Node), and Redwood Console (dashboards, rollouts UI). Does NOT include Dedicated capacity provisioning or Private on-prem install agents (those get a follow-up playbook but some patterns will be reused).

Deliverables:
- A compatibility grid mapping supported combinations (runtime binary versions, API contract versions, SDK minors, console UI) and their expected interoperability mode (forward-compatible, requires client update, partial fallback).
- Upgrade safety checklist (preflight, canary, ramp, metrics to observe, rollback triggers).
- Minimal automation requirements for the upgrade controller: preflight checks, traffic shaping, per-customer staged percentages, automated rollback on SLO regressions.
- Documentation links and runbook sections to embed in the release playbook and Console rollout flow.

Key design constraints and principles:
- Backwards-compatible read paths where feasible: older SDKs must continue to work against newer runtime for N-1 API changes unless explicitly breaking.
- Fail-open user experience for non-critical features; fail-fast for malformed requests.
- Small, observable canaries with automatic guardrails: 0% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automated pauses.
- Clear deprecation windows when breaking changes are unavoidable; automated deprecation notices surfaced in Console and via SDK warnings.

High-level compatibility matrix (summary):
- runtime-1.x with api-2.x: supported for gen/chat/embeddings with feature flags for streaming compatibility.
- api-2.5 introduces structured output schema v2: SDKs <3.1 will receive legacy JSON fallback with a warning header.
- console-2026.03 is UI-compatible with runtime-1.18+; older runtimes show a read-only mode for rollout controls.

Safety checklist (short):
1) Preflight: schema/payload validation tests, migration dry-run, binary-level compatibility smoke tests.
2) Canary: deploy to isolated pool, route 0.5%->5% of real traffic for 1 hour, run production prompt set, check latency, 99P latency, token cost delta, error rates.
3) Ramp: 5% -> 25% over 6 hours if metrics pass.
4) Full: automated checks pass for 24 hours at 25% then proceed to 100% with monitoring.
5) Rollback triggers: error rate +0.5% absolute, 99P latency +40% relative, any user-facing exception spike, structured-output mismatch rate >0.2%.

Automation requirements:
- Upgrade controller accepts target version + rollout policy; performs preflight, creates canary pool, configures traffic weights, monitors SLOs, and can execute automated rollback.
- Console needs API endpoints to control staged percentages and surface preflight results and guardrail alerts.
- SDKs should implement opt-in warnings for deprecated endpoints and expose a diagnostics hook for automated tests.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- How strict should the schema compatibility enforcement be for streaming vs non-streaming endpoints? (proposal: strict for structured streaming, lenient for legacy text streaming with warnings).
- Do we require SDKs to bundle compatibility shims or push users to upgrade (tradeoff: developer friction vs platform complexity).

Acceptance criteria:
- Published compatibility grid in Confluence and a JSON artifact generated by the upgrade controller.
- Automated preflight runner integrated with CI that performs the smoke tests listed above.
- Console UI surfaces staged rollout controls and shows guardrail status.

Notes: This ticket covers the design and gating criteria; separate implementation tickets will be created for the upgrade controller, Console integration, SDK warnings, and CI preflight jobs.

2026-03-11 - Performance test results: canary pool 3 passed within thresholds for latency and cost. Observed small KV cache warmup penalty (~3% tokens). Decided to add a warmup step to preflight called 'kv-prime' to reduce the initial penalty.
2026-03-12 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6189 implements preflight binary smoke harness and exposes metric hooks. Requesting review from infra-team.
2026-03-13 - Ops note: added suggested rollback automation thresholds to avoid manual escalation during off-hours. Ops prefers a conservative default (pause at 5% if any signal breaches).
